title: Vyukov's bounded queue, per-slot sequences
body: Each slot carries a sequence that says free for a position, published for it, or freed for the next lap; producers claim positions by compare-and-swap on one shared position.
rationale: A shared tail alone cannot be advanced by two producers without both seeing one slot free; the per-slot sequence is the long-published design (D. Vyukov's bounded MPMC queue), not a new invention.

title: One consumer, no compare-and-swap on its side
body: Only one thread pops, so the consumer's position is a plain field and pop is straight-line code; the MPMC generality of the algorithm is not used.
rationale: The customer has one writer per environment; a CAS on the consumer side would be cost for nothing.

title: Power-of-two capacity, at least two
body: The capacity must be a power of two (a mask addresses the slot) and at least 2 (one slot aliases published and free).
rationale: A mask instead of a division on every hand-off; the sequence states must stay distinct.

title: 64-bit positions, an unsigned comparison
body: Positions and sequences are uint64_t, compared by their modular difference against UINT64_MAX / 2 (MPSC_SEQ_IS_NEGATIVE), the trick of TCP sequence numbers; it replaced a signed cast.
rationale: A signed conversion is implementation-defined before C23 and would contradict the header's 'wrap-safe'; the true differences are bounded by the capacity.

title: Two allocation modes, one control
body: mpsc_ring_init_into() builds the ring in the caller's memory and never allocates; mpsc_ring_init() is a calloc of mpsc_ring_storage_size() bytes and a call to it; mpsc_ring_storage_size() includes the worst-case slack of both alignments.
rationale: A static or arena caller and a convenient caller share one code path; the caller never reasons about the library's alignment.

title: The two positions on separate cache lines
rationale: The producers' CAS traffic and the consumer's stores must not serialise each other through one line.

title: Refuse lock-backed atomics
body: Creation probes enqueue_pos and a slot's sequence with atomic_is_lock_free and refuses the ring; the project's builds also define MPSC_REQUIRE_ALWAYS_LOCK_FREE for a compile-time refusal.
rationale: C11 allows a lock behind _Atomic uint64_t; a lock would make the producers block silently.

title: A relaxed compare-and-swap
body: The claim's compare-and-swap on enqueue_pos is relaxed on success and failure; the ordering is carried by the slot's sequence, acquired before the claim and released after the store.
rationale: The CAS only decides who owns a position; the data's visibility is the sequence's job, so the cheapest CAS is enough.

title: An opaque void* payload, NULL storable
body: The ring stores void* and knows nothing of what it points to; NULL is stored and popped like any value.
rationale: The customer carries pointers to its job structures; the sibling SPSCring carries int descriptors.

title: Accept the claim-to-publish window
body: The ring is not made formally lock-free: a producer stalled between its claim and its publish holds back delivery; the window is a store and a release, no call, and the header says so.
rationale: A lock-free MPSC queue costs more on every hand-off for a guarantee the customer does not need (its submitters do not stall inside the window, SSS-005).
